small_guidance:
- The conv dominates runtime here (B=1024, OC=16, output spatial = 13×29×29 ≈ 10933, kernel 4³=64). The post-conv fused kernel is already cheap; tuning BLOCK_S further won't close the gap. If staying small, add configs with BLOCK_S=10933 padded to next pow2 (16384) and num_warps=16/num_stages=3 plus a CPG-aware layout — but expected gain is <10%.
- Try persistent single-chunk variant: since S≈10933 fits in one BLOCK_S=16384 tile, eliminate the chunk loop entirely (one load, one set of reductions) to remove loop overhead and let the compiler schedule better.
- Use `tl.rsqrt` instead of `1.0 / tl.sqrt`, and load gamma/beta once outside any loop (already done) — minor.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv3d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (B, OC tile, output-spatial tile). With OC=16 (tiny), tile OC=16 fully and tile spatial dim with BLOCK_M=64/128; GEMM-K = IC·kD·kH·kW = 3·64 = 192, small enough for a single K-loop. This is where the headroom is — conv is currently the bottleneck at ~7ms.
- Fuse HardSwish + GroupNorm partial reductions (per-channel sum, sumsq) into the conv epilogue: each conv program writes its output tile and also atomically accumulates per-(B,group) sum/sumsq into a small workspace. Then a tiny second kernel finalizes mean/rstd and applies affine + spatial-mean to produce (B,C). This avoids re-reading the full conv output.
- Alternatively, since output spatial (10933) >> OC (16), use channels_last layout for the conv output and have one program per (B, spatial tile) produce all 16 channels — then the post-conv reduction becomes a contiguous channel-inner reduction with coalesced loads.
